html:
Henry Morgan was a Welsh buccaneer who led raids from Port Royal against Spanish towns in the 1660s and 1670s, and later became deputy governor of Jamaica.

With commissions from the English governor, he sacked Puerto Principe in Cuba, Portobelo and Maracaibo, and in 1671 crossed the isthmus to burn Panama City. England and Spain had just made peace, so he was sent to London under arrest, but was knighted instead.

Back in Jamaica he grew rich as a planter and turned against the buccaneers he had led. He died at Port Royal in 1688, four years before the earthquake sank it. His name lives on in legend and on a rum label, in the age of the pirates.
